title: GitHub Wasn't Scanning Your Supabase Keys
caption:
I've never once checked whether GitHub actually scans my private repos.

On October 5 it added detectors for supabase_oauth_access_token, supabase_scoped_personal_access_token, lovable_api_key and two Pydantic tokens. Lovable joined the partner program too, so one of its keys found in a public repo gets forwarded to Lovable to revoke. A Supabase token only raises an alert — the rotating is yours.

The part I keep forgetting: secret scanning is on by default for public repos only. The private repo I actually build in gets nothing unless it's an org on GitHub Team with Secret Protection.

Public or private — where does your Supabase key live?
